it-2004-it-31.approach: An argument $P\rightarrow C$ is valid iff no assignment makes all premises true and the conclusion false. Try to build such a counterexample for each.

steps.title: Argument 3
steps.body: Take $q=F, p=T, r=F$: $(q\wedge r)\rightarrow p=T$, $\neg q\wedge p=T$; conclusion $r=F$ ⇒ **invalid**.

steps.title: Argument 4
steps.body: $p$ and $p\rightarrow r$ give $r$ (modus ponens); $q\vee\neg r$ with $r$ gives $q$ (disjunctive syllogism) ⇒ **valid**.

optionAnalysis.reason: Argument 2 is invalid ($p=F,q=T,r=T$).
Argument 3 is invalid ($p=T,q=F,r=F$).
